results.summary: This design implements a colorful version of the 2048 sliding tile puzzle game. It outputs a VGA video signal and accepts directional inputs from a keyboard or game controller to move the tiles. The design is intended to be run on an FPGA, such as the Tiny Tapeout FPGA, and requires a VGA display and input device. It was successfully tested on the TT FPGA with a game pmod, and a VGA playground link is provided for simulation.

This is an analog folded cascode operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with an NMOS input pair. It has four analog pins: VINN, VINP, VBIAS, and VOUT. The design is a transistor-level analog block, but the documentation provides only a one-line description and pin names, with no details on biasing, performance, or testing. Therefore, it is not possible to describe its operation or external requirements beyond the pin functions.

TinyQV is a small RISC-V SoC implementing the RV32EC instruction set with Zcb and Zicond extensions, using QSPI flash for program storage and QSPI PSRAM for data memory. It includes peripherals such as UART, SPI, a game controller interface, and an R2R DAC, many contributed by the community. The design is intended to be used with a QSPI PMOD containing flash and RAM, and can be tested by loading an image into flash and following a specific reset sequence. Notable features include its compact size, custom toolchain, and integration of analog output.

This design contains analog and custom layout experiments, primarily a current-starved ring oscillator VCO and a DAC, with digital test outputs and VGA signals. The VCO frequency is controlled by an analog input voltage and can be monitored directly or through divided digital outputs. Testing requires a precision variable voltage source and an oscilloscope to observe oscillation and frequency changes. The documentation provides detailed test steps and expected behavior, indicating it is an experimental analog block for the TT GF analog shuttle.

This is an analog factory test structure for GF180mcuD, consisting of large current mirror loads that draw a multiplied reference current from selected power rails. It includes sense wires to measure voltage drops on power rails and voltage raise on the VGND rail. Testing requires a programmable current source and a precision multimeter to provide the reference current and measure the sense voltages. The design is intended for characterizing analog support on the GF180mcuD process.

This design counts continuously and broadcasts the counter value every second over 100Mbps Ethernet using an application-specific Ethernet type. It reuses the Teapot Ethernet accelerator wrapper and requires an external Ethernet PHY PMOD with a LAN8720A and a 50MHz oscillator. The design autonomously sends packets, and testing involves connecting it to a local network and monitoring the packets. The project humorously aims to count until the heat death of the universe.

This design generates a VGA video signal showing a waving Philippine flag in a DVD-like screensaver style, with the text 'PILIPINAS' in a 7-segment style at the bottom. It requires a VGA display to view the output. The documentation is minimal, providing only the title and a brief description, with no details on implementation or testing beyond the visual output. It is a simple visual demo.

This is an analog voltage buffer designed to buffer a voltage signal and drive an off-chip probe. It has three analog pins: input, bias, and output. Testing requires biasing the amplifier with a 5uA current, applying a test signal to the input, and measuring the buffered signal at the output using an oscilloscope or multimeter. The documentation is brief but provides enough information for basic operation.

This design is a 256x8 SRAM intended for testing purposes, though only the top 128 entries are addressable. It has 6 address bits, 8 write data bits, and 8 read data bits, with a write enable signal. The SRAM is cleared on reset, and inputs and outputs are flopped once. No external hardware is required, and testing involves writing and reading data according to the provided pin functions.

Tiny FABulous FPGA is a small FPGA fabric with 64 LUT4+FF logic cells, configurable via a bitbang interface, and designed for use with Yosys and nextpnr. It provides 26 I/O buffers, global buffers, and a system reset, and can implement simple Tiny Tapeout designs directly. The bitstream is uploaded while reset is applied, and no external hardware is required. The design is notable for being a fully open-source FPGA fabric on a Tiny Tapeout tile.
